justifications.functional_suitability: All requirements are met: Fraud Scoring Engine scores transactions, Case Management Service handles reviews, and Model & Rule Hot-Reloader supports zero-downtime rule/model updates.
justifications.performance_efficiency: In-memory ONNX Runtime inference, ElastiCache Redis caching, reactive Spring WebFlux, and asynchronous event offloading to SQS provide concrete mechanisms to hit the sub-50 ms P99 target at 3,000 RPS.
justifications.compatibility: Interactions with the Payment Gateway (HTTP/2), IdP (OIDC/OAuth2), and ML Platform are well modeled. However, the Card Networks / Tokenization Vault defined in Context is absent from Container and Component levels.
justifications.usability: The Analyst Frontend provides tailored, explicit views including Case Dashboard & Queue, Decision & Audit Inspector, and Rule Simulation & Testing Sandbox for fraud analysts.
justifications.reliability: Resilience4j Circuit Breaker & Fallback Manager handles degraded scoring, while Aurora Multi-AZ and DLQs protect against message loss, though explicit gateway fail-open behavior during complete engine failure is unspecified.
justifications.security: Features AWS WAF, TLS 1.3, KMS TDE, PostgreSQL RLS, and S3 Object Lock. However, tokenization workflows and PAN masking mechanisms from R-05 are only minimally referenced in sanitization logic.
justifications.maintainability: Responsibilities are cleanly split between scoring, case workflows, and audit. Using managed AWS services (Fargate, Aurora, ElastiCache) makes the operational burden viable for a three-engineer team.
justifications.portability: Core application services use portable containers (Spring Boot, NestJS, ONNX), though deep coupling to proprietary AWS primitives (DynamoDB, S3 Object Lock, SQS) limits deployment outside AWS.

PERF-01.justification: Non-blocking Spring WebFlux, in-process ONNX runtime inference, and ElastiCache Redis feature caching ensure P99 latency remains well below 50 ms under 3,000 rps, while audit logging is fully decoupled asynchronously via Spring Events and SQS.
sensitivity_points: Redis network latency under high connection concurrency
tradeoffs: In-memory ONNX execution prioritizes minimal latency over complex multi-model ensemble pipelines

PERF-02.justification: The Case Management Service runs on dedicated ECS Fargate tasks and reads from Aurora Read Replicas and PgBouncer, completely isolating analyst query workloads from the real-time scoring engine and Redis cache.
sensitivity_points: Read replica replication lag under heavy case query loads
tradeoffs: Maintaining Aurora read replicas increases monthly infrastructure cost to ensure scoring performance isolation

AVAIL-01.justification: Resilience4j circuit breakers handle internal component degradation within the scoring engine, but if the scoring container itself crashes entirely, the architecture lacks an ALB-level or gateway-level fallback routing mechanism to prevent blocked requests within one minute.
sensitivity_points: ALB target group health check failure detection speed
tradeoffs: Local in-process circuit breaking avoids external dependencies but cannot recover from full container failures

AVAIL-02.justification: Scoring decisions emit audit events asynchronously to Amazon SQS via Spring Events. Slowness or outages in Audit Storage (S3 Object Lock / Lambdas) are buffered safely in SQS queues and DLQs without impacting scoring latency or dropping logs.
sensitivity_points: SQS queue retention duration during prolonged audit store downtime
tradeoffs: Asynchronous audit buffering guarantees scoring availability but introduces slight eventual consistency for audit queries

MOD-01.justification: The Model & Rule Hot-Reloader continuously polls the S3 Artifact Repository and dynamically swaps versioned ONNX/LightGBM binaries in memory without restarting tasks. Rollback is achieved within minutes by reverting the S3 version pointer, with all outputs stamped with the model version.
sensitivity_points: Polling interval of S3 model artifact updates
Memory overhead during concurrent model binary loading
tradeoffs: In-memory hot swapping ensures zero downtime but temporarily doubles per-task memory usage during reloads

MOD-02.justification: Rule artifacts are dynamically reloaded via the Hot-Reloader and evaluated without downtime, and explanations record applied rules. However, if a new rule requires novel velocity features not already computed in Redis or DynamoDB, feature pipeline changes are required.
sensitivity_points: Availability of underlying features in Redis for newly configured rules
tradeoffs: Dynamic rule parsing offers rapid activation but is constrained by pre-existing feature schema

SEC-01.justification: PCI-DSS tokenization and data sanitization within the Case Management Core prevent card numbers from being exposed to analysts. However, the architecture specifies no security monitoring, UEBA, or automated alerting mechanism to detect and alert on anomalous analyst access within 15 minutes.
sensitivity_points: Absence of automated access anomaly detection pipelines
tradeoffs: Strict data sanitization minimizes data breach blast radius but adds processing overhead on reads

SEC-02.justification: Decisions and explanations are persisted to Amazon S3 Object Lock in Compliance Mode with a 7-year retention period. The Audit Indexer in DynamoDB and Audit Query Service allow deterministic retrieval and cryptographic hash verification well within one working day.
sensitivity_points: Integrity of cryptographic hashes stored alongside Object Lock payloads
tradeoffs: WORM compliance storage prevents premature deletion but incurs ongoing storage retention costs
